claim_original: Chinese OEMs priced 20–35% below Indian equivalents for solid-fuel package boilers in SEA
methodology_note: UN Comtrade / World Bank WITS export unit values (USD/kg) used as primary price proxy. HS codes: 840211 (watertube boilers >45 t/h steam) and 840290 (other vapour generating boilers). Both sub-codes cover industrial solid-fuel package boilers. Two levels analysed: (1) global export unit values China vs India; (2) destination-specific bilateral imports Indonesia and Thailand from China vs India.

hs_840290.note: In Indonesia's bilateral data China is actually ~7% MORE expensive than India for this HS sub-code in 2023 — likely reflecting higher-specification units in Chinese export mix to Indonesia
hs_840290.note_thailand: In Thailand, China is ~27% MORE expensive than India, inverting the claim direction for this sub-code

data_tables.interpretation: Global unit-value data (China's blended export pool vs India's blended export pool) shows China 13–35% cheaper depending on HS sub-code and year. However, destination-specific bilateral flows do NOT confirm the direction uniformly — in Indonesia and Thailand in 2023, Indian HS 840290 exports arrived at lower unit values than Chinese exports, possibly because Indian shipments to these markets are predominantly lighter/smaller-capacity units. The global-level gap (particularly HS 840211 watertube: China $5.22/kg, India $8.08/kg) is the strongest signal for the larger-capacity solid-fuel package boilers claim is referencing.

new_sources.key_data: HS 840290 global exports 2023: China $3.94/kg vs India $5.06/kg — India 28% higher unit value, China ~22% cheaper
HS 840211 global exports 2023: China $5.22/kg vs India $8.08/kg — India 55% higher unit value, China ~35% cheaper for watertube boilers
HS 840290 global exports 2022: China $3.95/kg vs India $4.52/kg — India 14% higher unit value, consistent direction over two years

new_sources.publisher: World Bank WITS / UN Comtrade bilateral
new_sources.key_data: Indonesia 2023 imports HS 840290: from China $6.62/kg, from India $6.19/kg — in bilateral destination data, direction is reversed (India cheaper), complicating simple claim

caveats: HS 840290 is a parts-and-components sub-code that may dilute complete-boiler pricing signals
HS 840211 is specifically watertube boilers >45 t/h steam capacity — closest to large solid-fuel package boilers; this sub-code shows the strongest China price advantage (35%)
UN Comtrade unit values mix product types of varying specification within the HS code — a Chinese export with more basic specs will show lower $/kg even controlling for size
Bilateral destination flows (Indonesia, Thailand) show less consistent direction — China may be exporting higher-spec boilers to these markets explaining higher unit values
The claim is about 'solid-fuel package boilers' specifically — HS 8402 is the best available public proxy but includes fire-tube, watertube, and combined boilers of multiple fuels

suggested_revision: Based on global export unit-value data from UN Comtrade/WITS (primary multilateral source), Chinese OEM export prices for industrial boilers (HS 840211, 840290) are 15–35% below Indian equivalents on a USD/kg basis in global markets, with the gap widest for large-capacity watertube boilers (HS 840211: China $5.22/kg vs India $8.08/kg in 2023 = 35% lower). Destination-specific bilateral data for Indonesia and Thailand does not uniformly confirm the direction, suggesting the price gap is most visible in global export-pool averages rather than consistently at point-of-delivery in SEA. Revised claim: 'Chinese OEMs export industrial boilers at approximately 15–35% lower unit values than Indian equivalents (UN Comtrade/WITS HS 840211, 840290 data 2022–2023), though the actual landed-price gap in SEA procurement may be narrower due to product-mix differences.'

confidence_assessment.rationale: The directional claim (China cheaper than India) is now anchored to two years of primary UN Comtrade data across two HS sub-codes. The 20-35% range in the original claim is consistent with the global unit-value spread (13-35% across sub-codes and years), particularly the watertube sub-code hitting 35% in 2023. However, destination-specific SEA bilateral data shows a mixed picture, and the unit-value method cannot control for product specification mix. Confidence is Medium, not High, because: (1) no OEM filing or procurement-tender data found to cross-validate; (2) bilateral SEA flows show China sometimes arriving at higher prices than India, complicating the claim.
